full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque J: This Rule was issued at the instance of the accused-petitioner Abdur Rahman MolIah, elected Chairman of Paroly Union Parishad, calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why he should not be enlarged on anticipatory bail in Kalia PS Case No.17 dated 27-2-98 which gave rise to GR Case No.31 of 1998. 

 2. Informant Mohammad Moktel Shaikh lodged a First Information Report on 27-2-98 with Kalia Police Station alleging that on 26-2-98 his cousin Delwar Hossain was assaulted by the accused persons resulting in serious injuries to him and informant got him admitted in Noapara Hospital and was trying to obtain medical certificate. At this accused persons including the petitioner became annoyed with him. On 27-2-98 at about 12 noon while he along with his cousin victim Sukur Shaikh reached Wapda embankment by the southern side of Khararia Bazar accused-petitioner armed with bhela in his hand and accused Sharfuddin Molla also armed with a bhela in his hand and accused Rustom Molla came from behind and the petitioner abused the informant calling him, "Son of pig, you are going to bring certificate to start case? You will be finished" and having seen this informant started running forward. Then his cousin Sukur Shaikh came to obstruct the accused petitioner when accused Rustom Mollah ordered saying "Catch hold of that son of pig". Hearing the same accused petitioner Abdur Rahman Mollah struck Sukur Shaikh on the left side of his belly with the bhola in his hand and caused severe bleeding injury. As a result Sukur fell down on the ground when the accused Sharfuddin struck Sukur on the right side of his chest with bhola in his hand causing bleeding injury. As a result of those injuries Sukur Shaikh died on he spot. 

 3. Case of the petitioner is that in the election held in 1997 his defeated rival was one Mohammed Ferdous, an activist of the ruling party Awami League of his locality and to retaliate his defeat in the election he had instigated the informant to implicate the petitioner in Kalia PS case No.17 dated 27-2-98 and also instigated his brother Jabair Hossain to be a witness in the case though the I petitioner is quite innocent having no involvement with the alleged offence as alleged in the First Information Report. 

 4. It is the further case of the petitioner that informant influenced the local administration and law enforcing agencies as well as the police to harass and humiliate the petitioner. So he has been apprehending harassment and arrest by the police seriously affecting his personal liberty and if they succeed he would suffer irreparable loss and harm and injury. It is the further case of the petitioner that Magistrate being controlled by the Government he apprehends that he would not be properly and legally dealt with and he has reasons to believe that the Magistrate would allow the prayer for remand made by the police to torture and humiliate him. 

 6. Learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that petitioner has been falsely implicated in the case by the informant at the instigation of the defeated candidate in the Chairman election not only to curtail his personal liberty but also to prevent him from performing his public functions as an elected Chairman. He further submitted that if the petitioner surrenders before the Magistrate he may be remanded to police custody under the influence of his adversary party to torture and humiliate him. So petitioner had no alternative but to surrender before this Court and this Court having granted ad-interim anticipatory bail the same should be confirmed. 

 8. Ground of the petitioner for his not   surrendering before the Magistrate on the allegation that Magistracy in under the control of the Executive   Government and, as such, he apprehended that he would not be properly and legally dealt with and prayer of the police for his remand to the police custody would be allowed by the Magistrate and he would be tortured and humiliated by the police appears to us to be unfounded in the absence of anything to show in support of the same. In the case of Atikullah Khan Masud vs. Slate reported in 15 BLD (AD) 14 it has been observed that contention of the appellant that the Magistrate was not independent in the exercise of judicial function was not correct 

 9. We have already noticed that there is specific allegation against the petitioner of attacking the informant with a Bhola, a sharp cutting weapon and inflicting blow on the left side of the belly of the victim with Bhola causing bleeding injury and resulting in his falling on the ground and co-accused Sharfuddin striking on the right side of his chest with a Bhola causing instantaneous death of the victim Sukur. The offence alleged against the petitioner is of causing murder of the victim in furtherance of the common intention with the help of the co-accused. Such offence is punishable with death or imprisonment for life under section 302 of the Penal Code. In the case of Golam Haider vs. Karim Box reported in 15 DLR (SC) 2 anticipatory bail was refused to the appellants of the said case on the ground that the offence under section 326 of the Code with which they were accused of was punishable with imprisonment for life. 

 10. Petitioner's allegation that he has been falsely implicated in the case under the influence of his defeated rival Mohammad Ferdous whose brother is a witness of the prosecution does not find support from the First Information Report except that his brother Jubair Hossain only accompanied the 'informant along with one Wahidul Islam to the police station and were present at the time of lodging the First Information Report. There is also nothing to show except the allegations made in the application before us that petitioner's defeated rival Mohammad Ferodus is an activist of the ruling party. There is also no allegation in the application of the petitioner that he is an activist of any other rival political party for which he is being victimised. Moreover, we can not lend credence to the mere allegations in the absence of anything to prima facie substantiate the same. 

 11. On going through the application filed by the petitioner and also hearing his learned Advocate we are not satisfied as to the cause of his non-appearance before the Magistrate. Moreover, the offence with which he has been accused of being punishable with death or imprisonment for life anticipatory bail cannot be granted though the petitioner is an elected Chairman. In the case of Mohammad Belayet Hossain Sharif vs. State reported in 18 BLD 172 being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 247 of 1998 one of us agreeing with another learned brother rejected the prayer for anticipatory bail with the following observations: 

 "But, in my opinion, this Court would be reluctant to exercise its discretion in favour of a person who cannot satisfy this Court by cogent reasons cause of his non-appearance before the Court below and grounds for enlarging him on bail Ordinarily when warrant of arrest is issued against a person or a person is wanted in connection with a non-bailable offence of serious nature he is not entitled to get anticipatory bail. Merely because, a person is respectable, influential or highly placed in the society by reason of his being rich or educated ,or politically connected or otherwise holding important post or office he cannot avoid due course of the law to appear before the courts below and use this Court as a substitute of the subordinate Courts. If this Court exercises its discretion in favour of such persons without being so satisfied that would be doing injustice to the bulk of the litigants whose cases are pending before this Court for years together and could not be heard due to the overburdening of this Court with unnecessary business which is within 'the domain of the Courts below"
